thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P0 - Serving runtime: repeated container restarts on gpu-pool-3 due to CUDA OOM during prefill. Affected clusters: gpu-pool-3 (us-west1). Customers with increased errors: acct-319, acct-714. Pager sent to @Ryan. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-prefill-oom

Marta: Seeing a surge of long prefill requests from a few partners — lots of historic messages + huge system prompts. Prefill sizes hitting ~98k tokens in a few cases. Containers hit OOM within 30-60s of prefill and restart.

Ryan: I’m on call, grabbing logs and pod state now.

Ryan: kubectl -n serving logs pod/serve-abc-123 -c runtime --tail 200

Ryan (logs): ```
[2026-03-15T18:10:12Z] RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.00 GiB (GPU 0; 24.00 GiB total capacity; 21.12 GiB already allocated)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/runtime/serve.py", line 412, in prefill
    kv_cache.reserve(prefill_size)
  File "/app/runtime/kv_cache.py", line 87, in reserve
    raise CUDAOOMError('prefill')
RuntimeError: CUDA OOM during prefill (token_count=98304)
-- Container exit code 137, restart_count: 3
```

Sahil: Metric view: prefill_count spikes correlate with errors. ~2% of requests are >80k tokens but are responsible for ~65% of OOM events. Link: https://grafana/redwood/d/gpu-prefill

Sahil: Short-term mitigation suggestions: 1) enforce hard prefill truncation at ingress (max_context -> 32k) 2) route large requests to lower-memory quantized variant 3) backpressure/429 for oversized prefill requests.

Anita: Pushing a quick feature-flag change to limit prefill tokens at the API gateway. Rolling to us-west1 only first. Command: 
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://console.internal/api/flags -d '{"prefill_max_tokens":32000, "scope":"us-west1"}'

Marta: Applying gating at the runtime too: adding a request-level check to drop prefill > 64k with a 429 and helpful error message. Will patch and release a hotfix branch now.

Ryan: Implemented temporary k8s pod toleration to reduce churn while we stabilize: kubectl patch deployment serve --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"stabilize":"true"}}}}}'

James: Support: drafting emails to the two impacted customers (acct-319, acct-714). Note: degraded throughput and occasional failed requests for very long conversations. ETA for customer notice sent in 15m.

Anita: Started a 20% traffic route to model variant v2-quant-small (less KV, lower memory) via router: 
POST /routing/api {"route":"/generate","percent":20,"target":"v2-quant-small"}

Marta: After the flag and routing change, OOM restarts dropped from ~3/min to ~0.2/min. Still seeing tail events (~1 every 10-20m) from older sessions pinned to previous model versions.

incident-bot: Incident owner assigned: Marta. Current incident phase: mitigation. Incident channel: #incidents. Handoff ETA request received.

Ryan: Handoff to Anita at 18:45 UTC — I need to sign off. Notes: mitigation active, tracing enabled for prefill errors, still some restarts on nodes with older image.

Anita: Acknowledged handoff. Next actions: 1) force-roll pods on gpu-pool-3 to pick up runtime patch (kubectl rollout restart deployment/serve -n serving) 2) add conservative OOM kill thresholds 3) notify infra to check for any GPU driver anomalies.

Anita: Rolling restart started. Watch command: kubectl get pods -n serving -l app=serve -w

Sahil: Also enabling memory autoreclaim (kernel settings) on the host via host-ops: sudo sysctl -w vm.drop_caches=3 on nodes flagged; infra aware.

Marta: Customer impact summary for incident timeline (for post-incident): 
- 18:10 UTC: first pager, containers restarting under prefill load
- 18:25 UTC: gateway flag applied to truncate prefill to 32k in us-west1
- 18:30 UTC: routing 20% to v2-quant-small started
- 18:40 UTC: rollback of noisy sessions and pod stabilization reduced restarts by ~90%
- 18:45 UTC: handoff to Anita (oncall)

James: Sent customer notifications at 18:55 UTC, included mitigation steps and ETA for full resolution.

Anita: We'll keep this incident open until no restarts for 2 hours and postmortem ready. Assigning owners: Marta (runtime fixes), Sahil (metrics and gating), Anita (rollout + infra liaison), James (customer comms).

Ryan: Thanks team, logging my notes in pager duty and runbook. I’m offline. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status: MITIGATION. Updates will be posted here. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-prefill-oom. Please add any logs/commands below for the postmortem.

Marta: Postmortem to include: root cause analysis (unbounded prefill KV allocation + large client-side prompts), why routing fallback didn't auto-trigger earlier, and improvements: 1) hard validators at gateway 2) adaptive prefill caching 3) smarter fallback routing by token_count.

Anita: Noted. Adding follow-ups to backlog and scheduling a blameless postmortem meeting tomorrow.

James: Closing note: customers acknowledged the mitigation and appreciate the quick response, will await final RCA.
